quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 40 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will enter the roadway ahead.
Stop completely, then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, check for other vehicles and pedestrians, and proceed when safe.

questions.question: When riding in a group, riders should:

options.text: Keep a safe distance between each rider.
Ride as close together as possible.
Not worry about spacing between riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a safe distance between each rider.
questions.explanation: Group riders should use a staggered formation. This lets riders stay together while keeping safe distances between bikes.

questions.question: When parked on the road, a motorcycle should:

options.text: Park at a 45 to 90 degree angle to the curb.
Park without touching the curb with the wheel or fender.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park at a 45 to 90 degree angle to the curb.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle should park at a 45 to 90 degree angle to the curb. A wheel or fender should touch the curb.

questions.question: If you lock your rear brake on a dry, paved road, you should:

options.text: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
questions.explanation: If you lock the rear tire on a dry, paved surface, keep it locked until you stop. You can control the motorcycle on good pavement even with a locked rear wheel as long as the bike is upright and going straight.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, you should:

options.text: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
Assume the driver already sees you.
Ride on the far left side of the lane.
Ride on the far right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Position your bike in the center of the lane so the driver sees you in their rearview mirror. This is where drivers look most often.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road hazards. This sign warns that a railroad crossing is coming.

questions.question: A wobble or shaking of the front wheel and handlebars is usually caused by:

options.text: Wrong tire pressure or uneven weight.
A loose front wheel on the frame.
Hitting something with the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wrong tire pressure or uneven weight.
questions.explanation: A wobble is when the front wheel and handlebars shake side to side. It usually happens because of improper weight distribution, wrong tire pressure, or unsuitable accessories.

questions.question: An engine will seize because of:
questions.explanation: An engine seizes when oil is low. Without oil, engine parts cannot move smoothly and the engine overheats.

questions.question: If a motorcycle rider takes a turn too fast, they may:

options.text: Have better control of the motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast can cause the rider to lose control. The motorcycle may drift into another lane or go off the road.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:
questions.explanation: Gloves improve your grip and protect your hands. Choose full-fingered gloves made of strong material.

questions.question: How can you make your motorcycle more visible to other drivers?

options.text: Use your headlight only at night or in poor visibility.
Add an orange tint to your headlight.

questions.explanation: The best way to help others see your motorcycle is to ride with your headlight on all the time.

questions.question: What can help you survive a crash?
questions.explanation: A helmet that meets DOT standards gives you the best head and neck protection. Wearing a good-quality helmet that is properly fastened is the most important thing you can do to survive a crash.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a blind intersection?

options.text: Stop at the stop line, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.
Ignore the stop line and move forward to get a better look.
Stop at the stop line and then proceed through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop line, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.
questions.explanation: Stop where the stop line or sign tells you to stop. Then move forward slowly and stop again just before the cross traffic lane. Lean forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while you look.

questions.question: How can you reduce tiredness on a long ride?

options.text: Limit how many hours you ride each day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Limit how many hours you ride each day.
questions.explanation: Take frequent breaks to rest, even if you don't feel tired. Most experienced riders don't ride more than six hours per day. Wind, cold, and rain make you tired faster, so dress to protect yourself from the weather.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black text or symbols. They warn drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that the road ahead will be slippery when it's wet.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Wear bright, reflective clothing whenever you ride, day or night.

questions.question: What separates traffic lanes moving in the same direction?
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean you cannot pass. Dashed white lines mean you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: What affects a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?
questions.explanation: A person's BAC is affected by three main factors: how much alcohol they drank, how fast they drank it, and their body weight.

questions.question: When riding in the left third of a lane behind a car, the driver can see you in their side mirror. What is a problem with this?

options.text: Most drivers look at their side mirrors less often than their rearview mirror.
Wind can prevent the side mirror from working.
Drivers should not use their side mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most drivers look at their side mirrors less often than their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Drivers check their side mirrors less often than their rearview mirror. When following a car, it is better to ride in the center of the lane where the driver is more likely to see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Change lanes to let them pass, or slow down to create more space ahead of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to let them pass, or slow down to create more space ahead of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, ride in a way that lets them pass. If you speed up, they may just tailgate you faster, which increases danger.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the right lane will end.

questions.question: You should flash your brake light to:

options.text: Tell other motorists that you are riding near them.
Help other motorists see your motorcycle while traveling in slow traffic.
Tell other motorists that you are going to slow down or stop where they don't expect it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell other motorists that you are going to slow down or stop where they don't expect it.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light to warn other drivers that you are slowing down. This is especially important before making a tight turn off a high-speed road or slowing down unexpectedly.

questions.question: Mirrors on motorcycles:

options.text: Have blind spots, just like cars.
Do not have blind spots because a motorcycle is usually smaller than a car

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots, just like cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like cars. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: The best way to stay out of trouble while riding a motorcycle is to:

options.text: Look well ahead of your motorcycle.
Ride at speeds faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look well ahead of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Look far ahead on the road to spot hazards early. This gives you time to react and avoid danger.

questions.question: To make it easier to be seen by other motorists, you should:
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors so other drivers can see you easily. This helps during the day and at night.

questions.question: Riding on ______ may provide poor traction.
questions.explanation: Poor traction can happen on wet pavement, snow, ice, gravel, lane markings, steel plates, and utility hole covers.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn your head, shoulders, and torso.

questions.explanation: Turn only your head to look through a turn. Keep your shoulders still and your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: To avoid confusing other drivers, you should:

options.text: Turn off your turn signal after you complete a turn or lane change.
Use your horn only in emergency situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your turn signal after you complete a turn or lane change.
questions.explanation: Turn off your signal when you finish turning or changing lanes. Leaving it on confuses other drivers.

questions.question: The front brake supplies about how much of a motorcycle's potential stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake is much stronger than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: If you get a flat tire while riding, you should:

options.text: Hold the handle grips firmly and stay off the brakes.
Shift your weight toward the good wheel and brake normally.
Brake on the good wheel while immediately pulling off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handle grips firmly and stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip the handlebars firmly and keep the motorcycle straight. Do not brake right away. Wait until the motorcycle slows down, then safely exit the road.

questions.question: When choosing a jacket for protection, it should:

options.text: Fit loosely and flap in the wind.
Fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind.
Not be made of leather or another sturdy material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind.
questions.explanation: Choose pants and a jacket made of leather or another sturdy material. They should fit snugly so they do not flap in the wind, but loosely enough to let you move freely.

questions.question: It is illegal to operate a motorcycle with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of:
questions.explanation: In California, people age 21 or older cannot operate a motorcycle with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. People under 21 cannot operate a motorcycle with a BAC of 0.01 percent or higher. It may be unsafe to ride even if you are under the legal limit.

questions.question: A passenger should sit:
questions.explanation: Passengers should always sit behind the operator and hold firmly onto the operator's waist, hips, or midsection. They may also hold onto handgrips if the motorcycle has them. Passengers should never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: A benefit of keeping space between you and other vehicles is that:

options.text: You can draft off other vehicles better.
You will have more time to react to other drivers' movements.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will have more time to react to other drivers' movements.
questions.explanation: Keep space around your motorcycle at all times. If a hazard appears, you will have more time to respond and more space to maneuver safely.

questions.question: Hearing protection is:
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can damage your hearing over time, even with a helmet. Use hearing protection every time you ride to help prevent hearing damage.

questions.question: How should a group of motorcyclists pass another vehicle?
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, a group of motorcyclists should pass one at a time. Each rider should finish passing before the next one begins.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast can cause a rider to:

options.text: Cross into another lane of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross into another lane of traffic.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast may cause a rider to cross into another lane or leave the road. Slow down before entering a turn or curve.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is on the back of slow-moving vehicles that travel slower than 25 mph, such as construction equipment, farm machinery, or horse-drawn vehicles.

questions.question: To work properly, an eye or face shield must:

options.text: Restrict side vision so you focus on the road ahead.
Not allow eyeglasses or sunglasses to be worn.

questions.explanation: An eye or face shield must be free of scratches, resist penetration, allow clear views to the sides, fasten securely, allow air to pass through to prevent fogging, and have room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: When riding over scored pavement in a work zone, you should:

options.text: Look down to see the changes in the road surface.
Keep your head and eyes up.
Stay to the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your head and eyes up.
questions.explanation: When riding over scored pavement in a work zone, keep your head and eyes up. Ride slowly, maintain a steady throttle, and do not fight the handlebars.
